user.title: Fuel Ledger
user.description:
Keeps the books for your heating oil: consumption, energy and heat for the Energy dashboard, stock and range of your tanks, deliveries with their price, heating value and CO₂. A few short steps follow: the burner (with a power meter also what runs behind it), the nozzle, the tanks. Everything can be changed later on the integration page.

There is no back button in these steps: if something went wrong, close the dialog and start again.

data_description.name: Name of the fuel store, e.g. heating oil.

burner.title: Burner
burner.description:
Where does the consumption come from? One of these, from best to roughest:

- **Oil meter:** a meter reading in L or m³. It measures, nothing is calculated.
- **Burner run time:** a counter in hours (or minutes, seconds) from the boiler or a smart plug script. Keeps counting while Home Assistant is down.
- **Burner on/off:** a binary sensor on while the burner runs. Fuel Ledger counts the run time itself.
- **Power of the heating:** a smart plug or meter in front of the boiler (W). Fuel Ledger recognises the burner in it, and the pumps if you tell their power.

data_description.entity_id: Oil meter, run time counter, binary sensor of the burner, or the power of the heating in W.

data_description.power_entity_id: Besides a run time counter or meter: the power of the heating in W. Fuel Ledger recognises in it whether the burner, the oil preheater and the pumps run, each as a sensor of its own.

nozzle.title: Nozzle
nozzle.description: The consumption is run time × nozzle throughput × correction factor. The nozzle is stamped on it (e.g. 0.50 GPH 60°) and usually in the maintenance record.

data_description.nozzle_gph: Throughput in US gallons per hour, as stamped on the nozzle.
data_description.factor: Empty: 1. Corrects what the nozzle and the pressure leave out. Can be changed later and measured from dipstick readings.

data_description.nominal_flow: Litres per hour, if you know it instead of the nozzle (replaces it).
data_description.pump_pressure: The pressure of the oil pump, from the maintenance record or the gauge. A higher pressure burns more.
data_description.test_pressure: The pressure the nozzle is rated at. Empty: 7 bar (100 psi).
data_description.burner_entity_id: On while the burner runs: gives a live flow rate for the Energy dashboard.
data_description.prepurge_s: Seconds after each start in which the fan runs but no oil burns. Taken off every start.

tanks.title: Tanks
tanks.description: Your tanks give the stock its fill level and the readings with a dipstick their litres. Several tanks of the same size are created at once (battery tanks); others can be added later on the integration page, also tanks of another shape.

data_description.tank_count: 0 or empty capacity: no tanks, only the stock.
data_description.stock: All tanks together, in litres. Empty: the stock starts with the next delivery. Price and heating value of what is in the tanks can be entered with the action "Set stock".
data_description.link: At the bottom: the levels are always the same, one reading tells all. Only through their suction pipes (T-piece): each tank keeps its own level, the burner draws from the fuller one first.

data_description.per_cm: For readings in cm: litres per cm of height of one tank (its base area in m² × 10).
data_description.residue: Litres at the bottom the burner cannot draw. The range ends there.

components.title: Behind the power meter
components.description: What runs behind the power meter, each with its typical power. The burner is enough to count its run time; with the others, each pump gets a sensor of its own. Read the powers from the meter's history: the power with only the circuit pump running, with the burner running, and so on. More components can be added later on the integration page.

data_description.burner_power: Watts while the burner runs (fan, oil pump, ignition), without the pumps.

data_description.base_power: What the boiler's control draws all the time.
data_description.preheater_power: Warms the oil for a few minutes before the burner starts.
data_description.circuit_pump_power: Moves the water through the radiators.
data_description.circulation_pump_power: Keeps hot water moving to the taps, often on a timer. Only if it is plugged in behind the meter.

error.not_an_input: Choose an oil meter (L, m³), a run time counter (h, min, s), a binary sensor or a power sensor (W).
error.not_cumulative: Choose a meter reading, not a momentary value.
error.nozzle_required: Enter the nozzle, or its throughput under "More accurate".
error.not_power: Choose a power sensor in W or kW.
error.burner_required: Enter the power of the burner: it is how the burner is recognised.

init.title: Fuel Ledger
init.description: Tanks are edited on the integration page, each through its own entry. The correction factor is an entity of its own.

burner.title: Burner
burner.description: Oil meter, run time counter, binary sensor or power of the burner. Another one starts counting from its next reading; what was booked stays.

data_description.power_entity_id: Besides a run time counter or meter: the power of the heating in W. The components behind it are entries on the integration page.

nozzle.title: Nozzle
nozzle.description: Changes count from now on; what was booked stays.

data_description.nozzle_gph: Throughput in US gallons per hour, as stamped on the nozzle.

data_description.nominal_flow: Litres per hour, if you know it instead of the nozzle (replaces it).
data_description.pump_pressure: The pressure of the oil pump, from the maintenance record or the gauge.
data_description.test_pressure: The pressure the nozzle is rated at. Empty: 7 bar (100 psi).
data_description.burner_entity_id: On while the burner runs: gives a live flow rate.
data_description.prepurge_s: Seconds after each start in which no oil burns.

fuel.title: Fuel and boiler
fuel.description: Changes count from now on; what was booked stays. Deliveries with an invoice set heating value and CO₂ of the oil in the tanks themselves.

data_description.efficiency: Heat per energy in the fuel, e.g. 0.9. The chimney sweep's flue gas measurement gives a good value. Empty: 0.9.
data_description.heating_value: kWh per litre of oil of unknown origin, until a delivery tells it. Empty: 10.0 (net calorific value of heating oil). Use the gross value (about 10.6) to compare with gas bills.
data_description.co2: kg CO₂ per litre of oil of unknown origin. Empty: 2.66.

data_description.low_percent: The low stock sensor turns on when the usable stock is at or below this share of the capacity.
data_description.range_days: Days of consumption the range is calculated from.
data_description.reading_accuracy_cm: How exactly you read the level, ± cm. Gives the uncertainty of the measured factor.
data_description.link: At the bottom: the levels are always the same, one reading tells all. Only through their suction pipes (T-piece): each tank keeps its own level, the burner draws from the fuller one first.

power.title: Power meter
power.description: The components behind the power meter (burner, pumps) are entries on the integration page, each with its typical power.

data_description.base_power: What the boiler's control draws all the time, in W.

error.not_an_input: Choose an oil meter (L, m³), a run time counter (h, min, s), a binary sensor or a power sensor (W).
error.not_cumulative: Choose a meter reading, not a momentary value.
error.nozzle_required: Enter the nozzle, or its throughput under "More accurate".
error.efficiency_range: The efficiency is a factor such as 0.9, not a percentage.
error.not_power: Choose a power sensor in W or kW.
error.burner_required: The power as input needs a burner among the components: add it on the integration page first.

tank.title: Tank
tank.description: Readings with a dipstick or a ruler are entered per tank with the action "Record level". Several tanks on one suction line count together.

data_description.shape: Upright walls: litres per cm below. A steel tank on its side and a manufacturer's table ask for their values in the next step.

data_description.per_cm: Upright walls only: litres per cm of height (base area in m² × 10).
data_description.offset_cm: The reading in cm when the tank is empty, if you measure from the floor: the bottom of the tank, or what it stands on.
data_description.residue: Litres at the bottom the burner cannot draw.
data_description.level_entity_id: A sensor of the fill level in cm, L or %. With one on every tank, the stock is measured instead of calculated.

table.title: Table of the manufacturer
table.description: One pair per line: height in cm and litres, e.g. `10: 95`. Between them it is interpolated.

error.not_a_level: Choose a sensor in cm, L or %.
error.level_needs_dimensions: A level in cm needs the litres per cm (or another shape).
error.invalid_table: One pair of numbers per line, with different heights, and more litres the higher.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Saved. Fuel Ledger is reloaded with the change.

component.title: Component behind the power meter
component.description: Fuel Ledger finds the combination of components whose typical powers add up closest to the measured power. Each component gets a sensor whether it runs and one for its power.

data_description.power: Watts while it runs, without the others.

data_description.on_delay_s: Seconds it has to show before it counts as running. Keeps a short peak (the ignition) from being taken for a pump. Empty: 60 for pumps, 0 for the rest.
data_description.off_delay_s: Seconds it has to be gone before it counts as stopped. Empty: 120 for pumps, 0 for the rest. The burner always stops at once.

error.last_burner: This is the only burner, and the power meter is the input: without a burner nothing is counted. Add another burner first.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Saved. Fuel Ledger is reloaded with the change.

entry_not_found.message: No Fuel Ledger entry with this ID.

entry_not_loaded.message: This Fuel Ledger entry is not loaded.

not_a_tank.message: Choose the device of a tank of Fuel Ledger.

no_measured_factor.message: There is no measured factor yet: it needs two readings of all tanks at the same points, with the burner running in between.

amount_or_level.message: Enter the amount delivered, the stock after the delivery, or both.

stock_unknown.message: The stock before the delivery is unknown: enter the stock after it as well.

level_below_stock.message: The stock after the delivery is below the calculated stock before it ({stock} L). Enter the amount delivered as well.

amount_needed.message: Price, energy and CO₂ of the invoice need the amount delivered: the stock before the delivery is unknown.

in_future.message: The time is in the future.

too_early.message: The time is before Fuel Ledger started counting: there is no consumption for it.

height_or_volume.message: Enter the level in cm or in litres, one of them.

tank_without_dimensions.message: {tank} has no dimensions to turn cm into litres: add litres per cm, or enter the reading in litres.

level_below_amount.message: The stock after the delivery is smaller than the amount delivered. Check both.

no_burner.message: The power meter is the input, but no component is the burner. Add a component of the kind Burner.

record_delivery.name: Record delivery
record_delivery.description: A delivery of oil: sets the stock and blends price, heating value and CO₂ with what was left in the tanks. Enter the totals as on the invoice.

level_after.name: Stock after
level_after.description: Litres in all tanks after the delivery. With the amount as well, the rest before it is corrected.

energy.name: Energy content
energy.description: kWh, as on the invoice (in Germany required by the CO2KostAufG).

co2.name: CO₂
co2.description: kg CO₂, as on the invoice.

product.name: Product
product.description: E.g. heating oil EL low sulphur.

time.name: Time
time.description: When the oil was delivered. Empty: now. The new values count from the moment it is entered.

record_level.name: Record level
record_level.description: A reading of one tank with a dipstick or a ruler. Read all tanks one after the other: two such readings with the burner running in between give the measured factor.

volume.name: Litres
volume.description: Instead of the height, if you read litres.

point.name: Measuring point
point.description: Where you measured, e.g. front middle. Only readings at the same point are compared.

set_stock.name: Set stock
set_stock.description: Correct the stock without a delivery, e.g. to start with what is in the tanks, with price, heating value and CO₂ of that oil.

price.name: Price per litre
price.description: Of the oil in the tanks. Empty: unchanged.

components_alike.title: {entry}: two components draw almost the same power
components_alike.description:
Behind the power meter, these components draw so alike that Fuel Ledger cannot tell which of them runs: {pairs}.

The total stays right, and the burner is still counted correctly as long as it is not one of them. Only which of the two shows as running is a guess.

If you only want the burner's run time, remove one of them. If you know a more exact power for each, enter it with **Edit component**.
